title: Modal Dialog
summary: An overlay that takes focus, keeps Tab inside and makes the page behind inert.
description: Use `<dialog>` with `showModal()`: it makes the rest of the page inert and closes on Esc. Move focus inside on open, return it to the trigger on close, and name the dialog with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its title.

title: Disclosure
summary: A button that shows and hides a region, with aria-expanded telling its state.
description: The simplest show/hide: a `<button aria-expanded>` next to the content, or native `<details>`/`<summary>`. Pick it over Accordion when the sections are independent and don't need headings.

title: Accordion
summary: Stacked headings whose buttons each expand one panel.
description: Each header is a button inside a heading (`h3 > button[aria-expanded]`), so heading navigation still works. Panels may be `role=region` labelled by their header, but only when there are few, or the landmarks list floods.

title: Tabs
summary: A tablist of tabs with one visible tabpanel; arrow keys move between tabs.
description: Only the selected tab is in the Tab order (roving tabindex); ←/→ move and Home/End jump. `aria-selected` marks the active tab and `aria-controls` links its panel. Activate on Enter instead of on focus when panels are slow to load.

title: Menu Button
summary: A button that opens a menu of actions; aria-haspopup and aria-expanded announce it.
description: `role=menu` is for app-like command menus with arrow keys and typeahead, not for site navigation, which is a list of links in `<nav>`. Focus moves to the first item on open and back to the button on Esc.

title: Combobox
summary: A text input with a popup listbox; focus stays in the input while options highlight.
description: `aria-activedescendant` points at the highlighted option so it is announced without moving focus. `aria-expanded` sits on the input; `aria-autocomplete` says whether typing filters the list or completes inline.

title: Listbox
summary: A list of selectable options with one tab stop; arrow keys move, Space selects.
description: Use native `<select>` when you can: it works everywhere for free. A custom listbox needs `role=option` children, `aria-selected`, `aria-multiselectable` for multiple choice, typeahead, and a single tab stop.

title: Switch
summary: An on/off control announced as 'switch, on' that takes effect immediately.
description: Use `role=switch` with `aria-checked`, or `<input type=checkbox role=switch>`. Pick it over a checkbox when the change applies at once (settings), and over a toggle button when the label names a setting rather than an action.

title: Tooltip
summary: Short supplementary text on hover and focus, linked with aria-describedby.
description: Never the only label and never interactive. WCAG 1.4.13: it appears on focus as well as hover, stays while the pointer moves onto it, and closes on Esc without moving focus. Icon buttons still need their own name.

title: Breadcrumb
summary: A labelled nav with an ordered list of links; the last one has aria-current=page.
description: `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` wraps an `<ol>`, so screen readers announce how many levels deep you are. Draw separators with CSS or mark them `aria-hidden`. Showing where you are helps meet 2.4.8 Location (AAA).

title: Radio Group
summary: Pick one of several options; arrow keys move and select, Tab enters at the checked one.
description: Native `<input type="radio">` with a shared `name` inside a `<fieldset>` gives all of this for free. A custom `role=radiogroup` needs roving tabindex and `aria-checked`. Pick a select or listbox over it once there are more than about seven options.

title: Checkbox
summary: An independent on/off choice; 'mixed' marks a parent whose children are partly checked.
description: Space toggles it, Enter doesn't. `aria-checked="mixed"` (or the native `indeterminate` property, set from script) shows a 'select all' with some children checked. Pick a switch when the change applies immediately.

title: Slider
summary: Picks a value in a range; arrows step, Page Up/Down jump, Home/End go to the ends.
description: Native `<input type="range">` is the easy path. A custom `role=slider` needs `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` when the number alone means little. Pair it with a text field for exact values.

title: Spinbutton
summary: A number field with step buttons; ↑/↓ change the value and typing still works.
description: `role=spinbutton` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`. Native `<input type="number">` has quirks (it rejects some input silently), so plain text with `inputmode="numeric"` is often better for things like card numbers.

title: Toolbar
summary: A row of controls that takes one Tab stop; arrow keys move between them.
description: `role=toolbar` groups related controls, like a text editor's bold and italic buttons. It only pays off with three or more controls. Label it when a page has more than one, and set `aria-orientation="vertical"` if it runs top to bottom.

title: Tree View
summary: A nested list you expand and collapse; → opens or goes to the child, ← closes or goes up.
description: `role=tree` with `treeitem` children, each parent with `aria-expanded`. Only one tab stop; typeahead jumps by name. Pick it for file systems and outlines; for site navigation, nested lists of links are simpler and better supported.

title: Grid
summary: An interactive table: one tab stop, then arrow keys move from cell to cell.
description: `role=grid` suits spreadsheets and calendars, where cells contain controls. For data you just read, use a plain `<table>`: screen readers have table-reading commands that a grid replaces with focus moves.

title: Treegrid
summary: A grid whose rows expand like a tree: a file browser or email threads with columns.
description: `role=treegrid` combines grid navigation across cells with tree expansion on rows (`aria-expanded`, `aria-level`). It's the most complex APG pattern, so test it with real screen readers, and pick a tree or a table if either would do.

title: Feed
summary: A scrolling list of articles that loads more as you go; Page Down moves between them.
description: `role=feed` holds `role=article` children with `aria-posinset`, and `aria-setsize` (-1 if unknown). Set `aria-busy` while loading. Infinite scroll hides the footer, so give a way past the feed or use a 'Load more' button.

title: Carousel
summary: Slides shown one at a time; auto-rotation needs a pause button and stops on focus.
description: Previous and next are real buttons; each slide is a `role=group` with `aria-roledescription="slide"` and a label like '2 of 5'. Turn the live region off while it rotates. Most users never see slide two, so think twice.

title: Menubar
summary: A desktop-style bar of menus (File, Edit, View); ←/→ move between menus, ↓ opens one.
description: `role=menubar` with `menuitem` children that open `role=menu`. Only for app-like command menus; a site's navigation bar is a `<nav>` of links, and making it a menubar gives keyboard users the wrong keys.

title: Meter
summary: Shows a value within a known range: disk used, battery, password strength.
description: Native `<meter>` or `role=meter` with `aria-valuenow`, min and max. It isn't a progressbar, which tracks a task moving to completion. Add `aria-valuetext` ('Strong') when the number alone isn't the message.

title: Window Splitter
summary: A focusable divider between panes; arrow keys resize, Enter collapses and restores.
description: A `role=separator` that is focusable, with `aria-valuenow` (0–100) for the primary pane's size and `aria-controls` pointing at it. Dragging alone fails 2.5.7, so the keyboard and a collapse button matter.

title: Data Table
summary: A real <table> with a caption and header cells, so screen readers can read cell by cell.
description: Use `<th scope="col">` and `scope="row"`, and a `<caption>` as its name. A sortable column puts a button inside the `<th>` and `aria-sort` on the `<th>`. Never build data tables from divs: the table commands disappear.

title: Landmarks
summary: header, nav, main, aside and footer: regions screen reader users jump between.
description: They map to banner, navigation, main, complementary and contentinfo. Use one `<main>` per page and label repeated landmarks (two navs) with `aria-label`. A `<section>` only becomes a region landmark once it has an accessible name.

title: Button role
summary: Native <button> gives you the role, focus, Enter and Space for free.
description: `role=button` on a div only changes what is announced: you still owe `tabindex=0`, Enter and Space handlers and disabled behaviour. Use `<button type="button">` and style it however you like.

title: Alert role
summary: An assertive live region: interrupts the screen reader to announce at once.
description: For urgent, time-sensitive messages (session expiring, save failed). `role=alert` implies `aria-live=assertive`. Put the text into a container that is already in the DOM; a region inserted with its content may not be read.

title: Status role
summary: A polite live region for advisory messages like 'Saved' or '3 results'.
description: `role=status` waits until the user pauses. Prefer it to alert unless a delay would cause harm: too many interruptions and people stop listening. Use `role=log` for appended history such as chat messages.

title: Presentation role
summary: role=none strips an element's own semantics but keeps its content readable.
description: For layout tables or a list restyled as something else. It hides nothing (that's `aria-hidden`) and is ignored on focusable elements. Never put it on a real heading or button to tidy up announcements.

title: Alertdialog role
summary: A modal dialog that interrupts with an urgent message and needs a response.
description: Use `role=alertdialog` for 'Delete 3 files?' or 'Unsaved changes', not for ordinary dialogs. Point `aria-describedby` at the message so it's read on open, and focus the least destructive button (Cancel).

title: aria-label
summary: Names an element with a string when there is no visible label.
description: Good for icon buttons and repeated landmarks. It replaces the content as the name, page translators often skip it, and voice control users can't see it, so prefer a visible label. It's ignored on plain divs and spans.

title: aria-labelledby
summary: Names an element from the text of other elements, referenced by id.
description: It beats `aria-label` and native labels in the name computation. List several ids to join them in order ('Delete' + row title); hidden elements can be referenced. Use it for dialogs, regions and tables titled by a visible heading.

title: aria-describedby
summary: Adds secondary text, like a hint or an error, read after the name and role.
description: Point it at help text, a format hint or an error message so it's announced on focus. It's a description, not a name: keep it short, because it is read every time. Pair it with `aria-invalid` on a field that failed validation.

title: aria-hidden
summary: Removes an element and its children from the accessibility tree.
description: For decorative icons and duplicated content. It doesn't stop focus: an `aria-hidden` button can still be tabbed to and is announced as nothing. To take a region away from everyone, keyboards included, use `inert` or `hidden`.

title: aria-expanded
summary: Says whether what a control opens is open: 'collapsed' or 'expanded'.
description: It goes on the button, not the panel. Use it for disclosures, accordions, menu buttons and comboboxes, and update it on every toggle: a stale value is worse than none.

title: aria-pressed
summary: Makes a button a toggle, announced as 'pressed' or 'not pressed'.
description: Keep the label constant ('Mute') and flip `aria-pressed`; changing the label to 'Unmute' as well reads as 'Unmute, pressed'. Use a switch for a setting, and a radio group when only one of several can be on.

title: aria-current
summary: Marks the current item in a set: the page, step, date or location.
description: `aria-current=page` on the active nav link, `step` in a wizard, `date` in a calendar. It isn't `aria-selected`: current is where you are, selected is what you've picked inside a widget like tabs or a listbox.

title: aria-live
summary: Asks screen readers to announce changes inside a region without moving focus.
description: `polite` waits for a pause, `assertive` interrupts. The region must exist before its text changes. `aria-atomic=true` reads the whole region instead of just what changed. Prefer `role=status` or `role=alert`, which set it for you.

title: aria-disabled
summary: Announces a control as unavailable but keeps it focusable.
description: Native `disabled` takes a button out of the Tab order, so keyboard users never learn it exists or why. `aria-disabled=true` keeps it reachable and readable, but you must block the action yourself. Good for a Submit that explains what's missing.

title: aria-invalid
summary: Flags a field that failed validation; screen readers say 'invalid entry'.
description: Set it only once the user has tried (on blur or submit), never on an untouched form. Link the error text with `aria-describedby` and say it in words: a red border alone fails Use of Colour. Meets 3.3.1 Error Identification.

title: aria-controls
summary: Points from a control to the element it changes, by id.
description: Tabs link to their panels and comboboxes to their listbox with it. Many screen readers don't announce it, so it never replaces `aria-expanded` or a sensible DOM order. Add it where a pattern asks for it and don't rely on it.

title: aria-owns
summary: Makes elements elsewhere in the DOM children of this one in the accessibility tree.
description: A workaround for portals and popups rendered at the end of `<body>`. It can confuse focus order and isn't supported everywhere, so first try rendering the element in the right place. Never point two elements at the same child.

title: aria-busy
summary: Marks a region as updating, so assistive tech can wait before reading it.
description: Set it to `true` while a feed loads or a live region gets several changes, then `false` when done. Support varies, so don't let a region stay busy forever: some screen readers skip its content while it's set.

title: aria-errormessage
summary: Points a field at its error text; exposed only while aria-invalid is true.
description: Meant for errors as `aria-describedby` is for hints. Screen reader support still lags behind `aria-describedby`, so many teams reference the error from `aria-describedby` too. Either way, the error must also be visible.

title: aria-roledescription
summary: Replaces the spoken role name, such as 'slide' instead of 'group'.
description: Use it rarely, on an element that already has a valid role, for things with no ARIA role (a carousel slide). Renaming a button to 'clickable thing' hides the role users rely on to know what keys work. Translate it like other text.

title: aria-modal
summary: Tells assistive tech that everything outside this dialog is unavailable.
description: Goes on `role=dialog` or `alertdialog` to stop screen readers browsing behind it. It doesn't block mouse or Tab, so a custom modal still needs `inert` on the rest. Native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` is modal already.

title: aria-selected
summary: Marks the chosen item in tabs, listboxes and grids: 'selected'.
description: Selection is for items in a composite widget: a tab, an option, a gridcell. Checkboxes, radios and switches use `aria-checked` instead. Selection often follows focus in single-select lists; in multi-select ones it doesn't.

title: aria-haspopup
summary: Says a control opens a popup and what kind: menu, listbox, tree, grid or dialog.
description: `true` means menu. Screen readers announce it ('menu button'), so only use it when it really opens that type; a disclosure that reveals content inline doesn't need it. Pair it with `aria-expanded` to say whether it's open.

title: aria-valuetext
summary: A readable version of a range value: 'Monday' instead of 1, or '3 of 5 stars'.
description: Range widgets (slider, spinbutton, meter, progressbar) announce `aria-valuenow` as a bare number. When the number needs units or names ('$40', 'Medium'), set `aria-valuetext` and keep it updated with the value.

title: aria-keyshortcuts
summary: Announces the keyboard shortcut that activates an element, like Control+S.
description: It documents a shortcut; it doesn't create one, so you still handle the keys. Show the shortcut visually too (a tooltip or menu hint). Avoid single-key shortcuts or let users turn them off (2.1.4).

title: Accessible name
summary: What a screen reader announces for an element, computed from several sources.
description: Precedence: `aria-labelledby`, `aria-label`, the native label (`<label>`, `alt`, `<caption>`), the content for buttons and links, then `title`. Voice users say the name, so it must contain the visible label (2.5.3 Label in Name).

title: Roving tabindex
summary: One tab stop per widget: the active item has tabindex=0, the rest have -1.
description: Tab enters and leaves a toolbar, tablist or grid in one press; arrow keys move focus by swapping which item has `tabindex=0`. The alternative, `aria-activedescendant`, keeps DOM focus on the container and suits comboboxes.

title: Focus management
summary: Move focus on purpose when the UI changes, and give it back when you're done.
description: Open a dialog: focus inside it. Close it: back to the trigger. Delete a row: focus the next one. SPA route change: focus the new `h1`. Never leave focus on a removed element, or it drops to `<body>` and the user loses their place.

title: inert
summary: Makes a subtree unfocusable, unclickable and hidden from assistive tech.
description: Set `inert` on the page behind a custom drawer or modal instead of trapping Tab with scripts; `showModal()` does it for you. Unlike `aria-hidden`, it also blocks focus and clicks, so hidden content can't be reached by keyboard.

title: Skip link
summary: The first link in the tab order, jumping past repeated navigation to the content.
description: Visually hidden until focused, then shown at the top. Its target (`<main id="main" tabindex="-1">`) must take focus so the next Tab carries on from there. With landmarks and headings it meets 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks.

title: Visually hidden
summary: Hides text on screen but keeps it in the accessibility tree.
description: The clip and 1px pattern (`.sr-only`) adds context, like 'Edit profile'. `display:none`, `visibility:hidden` and `hidden` remove text for screen readers too. Don't hide focusable elements this way unless they appear on focus.

title: Focus indicator
summary: :focus-visible shows a clear ring for keyboards without flashing on mouse clicks.
description: Never `outline: none` without a replacement (2.4.7 Focus Visible). A 2px solid outline with 3:1 contrast against the background, offset from the control, works everywhere. Forced-colours mode drops box-shadow, so use outline.

title: Reduced motion
summary: Honour prefers-reduced-motion: swap big movement for fades, or for nothing.
description: Parallax, zooms and sliding pages can trigger vestibular disorders. Put motion inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so it's opt-in (2.3.3, AAA). Anything moving for over 5s needs a pause control (2.2.2, A).

title: Alt text
summary: Describe what an image means in context; use an empty alt for pure decoration.
description: `alt=""` skips decorative images; a missing alt makes some screen readers read the file name. Say what matters ('Sales up 20% in May'), not 'image of'. A linked image's alt names the destination. Charts also need a text or table version.

title: Form labels
summary: Every input gets a visible <label> that stays put while the user types.
description: A `<label for>` names the field and enlarges its click target. A placeholder is no label: it vanishes, often fails contrast and isn't reliably announced. Group radios and checkboxes in a `<fieldset>` whose `<legend>` asks the question.

title: Captions
summary: Synchronised text for the speech and meaningful sounds in a video.
description: Prerecorded video needs captions (1.2.2, A); live video needs them at AA. Name speakers and include sounds like [door slams]. Auto-generated captions are a draft, not a pass. A transcript also helps deafblind people and skimmers.

title: Contrast (Minimum)
summary: Text needs 4.5:1 contrast with its background; large text needs 3:1.
description: Large means 24px regular or about 18.7px bold. Disabled controls and logos are exempt. Check every state: hover, placeholder, text over images. Brand colours often fail on white, so ship a darker text token instead of fixing it page by page.

title: Contrast (Enhanced)
summary: AAA raises text contrast to 7:1, and 4.5:1 for large text.
description: Rarely required by law but worth hitting for body copy, long reading and dense data. Make it the target for your default text token, so only secondary and accent text sits between 4.5:1 and 7:1.

title: Non-text Contrast
summary: Input borders, icons, focus rings and chart parts need 3:1 against their neighbours.
description: If you need to see it to use the control, it needs 3:1: a text field's border, a checkbox's box, a switch's thumb, a focus ring. A light grey field border on white is the classic failure.

title: Use of Colour
summary: Colour is never the only way information is shown.
description: Error fields need an icon or text, not only red. Links in body text need an underline, or 3:1 against the text plus a hover cue. Chart series need patterns or direct labels. Check in greyscale: if the meaning disappears, add a second cue.

title: Reflow
summary: Content works 320 CSS px wide (400% zoom) without scrolling both ways.
description: A 1280px window zoomed to 400% is 320px wide: basically a phone layout, so responsive design mostly passes. Data tables, maps and diagrams are exempt. Size with rem and avoid fixed heights that clip text as it grows.

title: Target Size (Minimum)
summary: Pointer targets are at least 24×24 CSS px, or spaced so a 24px circle fits.
description: New in WCAG 2.2; links inside a sentence are exempt. For touch, the 44×44 AAA target (2.5.5), Apple's 44pt and Material's 48dp are better defaults. Grow the hit area with padding or a pseudo-element rather than the icon.

title: Keyboard
summary: Everything a mouse can do, a keyboard can do, with no timing required.
description: Unplug the mouse and Tab through: every control reachable, usable with Enter, Space or arrows, and never stuck (2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap). Click handlers on divs are the usual failure. Single-key shortcuts need a way to turn them off (2.1.4).

title: Focus Order
summary: The Tab order follows the visual reading order.
description: DOM order is focus order, so write the DOM in reading order and keep CSS reordering (flex `order`, grid placement) cosmetic. A positive `tabindex` jumps ahead of everything: never use one. Closed off-screen menus must leave the order.

title: Focus Not Obscured
summary: A focused control is never fully hidden by sticky headers, banners or chat widgets.
description: New in WCAG 2.2. The usual failure: Tab moves under a sticky footer or a cookie banner. Setting `scroll-padding` to the sticky bar's height keeps focus in view. AAA (2.4.12) asks that no part of it is hidden.

title: Name, Role, Value
summary: Every control exposes its name, role and state to assistive tech, and updates them.
description: Native HTML does it for you. A custom widget must set a role, an accessible name and states such as `aria-checked` or `aria-expanded`, and change them as it changes. Most ARIA attributes exist to satisfy this criterion.

title: Info and Relationships
summary: Structure you can see is also in the markup: headings, lists, tables and labels.
description: If it looks like a heading it's an `<h2>`; if it looks like a list it's a `<ul>`. Data tables use `<th>` with `scope`, and fields are tied to their labels. Bold text and line breaks tell a screen reader nothing.

title: Dragging Movements
summary: Anything done by dragging also works with a single tap or click.
description: New in WCAG 2.2. Sortable lists get up/down buttons or a 'Move to' menu, sliders accept a click on the track, maps have pan buttons. People using a head pointer or with a tremor can't press, hold and move. Freehand drawing is exempt.

title: Accessible Authentication
summary: Logging in never depends on remembering, transcribing or solving a puzzle.
description: New in WCAG 2.2. Allow paste and password managers, offer passkeys or email links, and don't split one-time codes into boxes that block paste. Object-recognition CAPTCHAs pass at AA but not at AAA (3.3.9).

title: Redundant Entry
summary: Don't make people type again what they already entered in the same process.
description: New in WCAG 2.2. Pre-fill billing from shipping or offer 'Same as above'. Re-entering a password for security is exempt. Add `autocomplete` attributes (1.3.5) so browsers can fill in the rest.

title: Language of Page
summary: Set <html lang> so screen readers read the text with the right voice and rules.
description: Without it, a Spanish page may be read with English pronunciation. Mark passages in another language with `lang` on their element (3.1.2, AA). Use a BCP 47 tag such as `en`, `es` or `pt-BR`; it also drives hyphenation and spell-check.

title: Meaningful Sequence
summary: When order matters, the code reads in the same order as the screen.
description: CSS can place a price before its product name visually while the DOM has them the other way. Screen readers and reflow follow the DOM. Keep source order equal to reading order, and check with styles turned off.

title: Sensory Characteristics
summary: Instructions don't rely only on shape, position, size or sound.
description: 'Click the round button on the right' fails for a screen reader user and anyone on a reflowed layout. Name the thing: 'Select Continue (the round button on the right)'. A beep alone can't be the only cue either.

title: Orientation
summary: Content works in portrait and landscape; don't lock the screen to one.
description: People with a tablet mounted to a wheelchair can't rotate it. Lock orientation only when it's essential, like a piano app or a cheque scanner. Test both, including on phones with the larger text setting.

title: Identify Input Purpose
summary: Fields about the user carry an autocomplete token so browsers can fill and label them.
description: `autocomplete="email"`, `given-name`, `tel`, `street-address`, `one-time-code`. Autofill saves typing and memory, and helps meet Redundant Entry. Use the exact tokens from the HTML spec; made-up values do nothing.

title: Audio Description
summary: Narration of what happens on screen when the soundtrack alone doesn't tell you.
description: Needed at AA for prerecorded video whose visuals carry meaning (1.2.5). Write the script so key visuals are spoken in the main audio, and you may not need a separate track. A text transcript with visual notes helps too.

title: Resize Text
summary: Text can be zoomed to 200% without content getting cut off or overlapping.
description: Size with `rem` and avoid fixed heights on containers that hold text. Never disable pinch zoom with `user-scalable=no` or `maximum-scale=1`. Respect the user's default font size by not setting `html { font-size }` in px.

title: Images of Text
summary: Use real text, not text baked into an image, unless it's a logo.
description: Text in an image blurs when zoomed, can't change colour or spacing, and can't be translated or searched. Web fonts and CSS can do nearly any visual treatment. Logos and essential cases (a font sample) are exempt.

title: Text Spacing
summary: Layout survives users widening line, paragraph, letter and word spacing.
description: Test with line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em and word spacing 0.16em (a bookmarklet applies them). Fixed-height buttons and cards clip text. Let containers grow with their content.

title: Character Key Shortcuts
summary: Single-key shortcuts can be turned off, remapped, or only work when the widget has focus.
description: Speech input types letters, so 'saying' a word can fire a dozen shortcuts in a row. Gmail-style one-key shortcuts need an off switch, or a modifier like Ctrl. Shortcuts limited to a focused component (a listbox's typeahead) are fine.

title: Timing Adjustable
summary: Time limits can be turned off, adjusted, or extended with a simple action.
description: A session timeout warns before it expires (at least 20 seconds ahead) and offers 'Stay signed in'. Exceptions: real-time events like auctions, limits that are essential, and limits over 20 hours. Save form progress anyway.

title: Pause, Stop, Hide
summary: Moving, blinking or auto-updating content lasting over 5s can be paused or hidden.
description: Carousels, tickers, animated banners and auto-refreshing feeds pull attention away from reading. Give a visible pause button, or stop after 5 seconds. Loading spinners are fine. Reduced motion is a different, AAA angle on motion.

title: Three Flashes
summary: Nothing flashes more than three times in any one second.
description: Flashing, especially saturated red, can trigger seizures in people with photosensitive epilepsy, and it's the one failure that harms people directly. Check videos and animations with a tool like PEAT, and avoid strobing effects.

title: Page Titled
summary: Every page has a <title> that says what it is, most specific part first.
description: 'Checkout – Payment – Shop' is what a screen reader reads first and what tabs and history show. In a single-page app, update `document.title` on every route change. Duplicate titles across pages are the usual failure.

title: Link Purpose
summary: Each link's text, with its context, says where it goes.
description: Screen reader users pull up a list of links, where ten 'Read more' links are useless. Write 'Read more about pricing', or add visually hidden text. An icon-only link needs an accessible name; a URL as text is hard to listen to.

title: Multiple Ways
summary: There's more than one way to find a page: navigation, search, a sitemap or links.
description: Different people find things differently: some browse, some search. A site search plus the main navigation usually passes. Steps inside a process, like checkout pages, are exempt.

title: Headings and Labels
summary: Headings and labels say what their section or field is about.
description: Info and Relationships asks that headings exist; this asks that they're useful. 'Details' and 'More' say little; 'Delivery address' says a lot. Clear headings let everyone skim, and screen reader users jump between them.

title: Focus Appearance
summary: The focus ring is at least a 2px outline with 3:1 contrast against the unfocused state.
description: AAA, but a good target for a design system's focus ring. A thin dotted outline or a faint colour change fails. A solid 2px outline offset from the control, in a colour that contrasts with the background, passes almost everywhere.

title: Pointer Cancellation
summary: Actions fire when the pointer is released, so a slip can be cancelled by moving away.
description: Trigger on `click` (pointer up), not `mousedown` or `touchstart`. People with tremors often press the wrong thing; releasing outside the target should do nothing. Drag and drop and piano keys are exempt when down-events are essential.

title: Label in Name
summary: A control's accessible name contains the words of its visible label, ideally at the start.
description: Voice control users say what they see: 'Click Search'. If an `aria-label` says 'Find products' on a button labelled 'Search', the command fails. Extend the visible text, don't replace it: 'Search products' works.

title: On Focus
summary: Moving focus to something never triggers a change of context by itself.
description: Tabbing onto a field must not submit a form, open a new window or move focus elsewhere. Keyboard users have to pass through elements to reach others. Showing a tooltip or a hint on focus is fine; navigation isn't.

title: On Input
summary: Changing a setting doesn't change context unless the user was warned first.
description: A select that navigates as soon as you pick an option traps keyboard users, who fire it by arrowing through the list. Add a Go button, or say beforehand what will happen. Filtering results in place is not a change of context.

title: Consistent Navigation
summary: Navigation repeated across pages stays in the same relative order.
description: Users learn where things are; moving 'Account' around breaks that, especially for people with memory or vision difficulties. Items can be added or hidden per page, as long as the shared ones keep their order.

title: Consistent Help
summary: Help options (contact, chat, FAQ) appear in the same place on every page that has them.
description: New in WCAG 2.2. People who get stuck need to find help without hunting. It doesn't require help to exist, only that what exists stays in the same relative order, like a footer 'Contact us' link on every page.

title: Error Suggestion
summary: When an error is detected and a fix is known, say how to fix it.
description: 'Invalid date' identifies the error; 'Enter the date as DD/MM/YYYY' fixes it. List the allowed values when there are few. Don't suggest anything when it would weaken security, such as which half of a login was wrong.
